messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT P0 — private-vpc-gpu-queue (#cust-acme-prod) queue length > 600 for 7m, 95th token latency > 3s, errors increasing. Pager: oncall infra.
Dmitri: oncall here, ack. landing now. any customer-facing impact noted? :eyes:
Sara: seeing steady 502s on the vpc gateway for that tenant, and a queue backlog in the cluster's gpu-provisioner. repro rate ~15rps failing to schedule pods. Logs attached in the dashboard (link).
Kevin: checking autoscaler events. `k get events -n cust-acme` shows repeated "failed to provision node: quotaExceeded" and a few image-pull timeout errors around same time.
Maya: I can run a quick describe on the nodepool. `kubectl describe nodepool acme-gpu-pool` -> shows desired=8 current=4, provisioning=2, but 2 stuck in Provisioning -> Init. cloud logs show subnet allocate timeouts.
Infra-Runner: Cloud error details: attempt to allocate ENIs failed for the two nodes due to secondary IP exhaustion in customer subnet (customer's CIDR is close to full). Also a few instances failed health checks because the init container can't reach our private registry (no NAT gateway in that subnet).
Dmitri: that matches "customer cluster constraints" — their private VPC has a very small subnet and no NAT. Autoscaler kept requesting nodes but cloud rejected. So scale limit for cluster reached, autoscaler entered backoff (sticky scaler behaviour).
Sara: customer impact: their prod routing to that model is causing slowdowns for some users (10% error rate on embeddings endpoint for that tenant). CS reported a ticket and flagged a dozen seats impacted.
Kevin: mitigation plan: 1) reduce routing to the affected model for that tenant (traffic split) 2) temporarily divert requests to fallback smaller model in hosted fallback pool 3) manual scale workaround: create ephemeral nodes in a different subnet (if allowed) or request customer's network changes.
Maya: I can flip the traffic split in the router: `/api/v1/routes/split` — reducing weight to 10% for that VPC. Will do now.
Maya: ```
# curl to update route
curl -XPOST https://console.internal/api/routes/split \
  -d '{"tenant":"cust-acme","model":"gpu-large","fallback":"gpu-small","weight":0.1}'
```
Maya: done — reduced to 10% to gpu-large; fallback to gpu-small at 90%.
Dmitri: good. also let's enable request-level throttling on the vpc ingress for that tenant to cap outstanding requests at 50 to avoid queue pileup.
Kevin: I'll push the throttle rule. `rbac update` -> applied. Now queue length trending down from 600 to ~220.
Infra-Runner: nodepool provisioning still stuck because of ENI exhaustion in their subnet. Tried to create nodes in alternative subnet but customer's cluster is pinned to specific subnets via their onboarding config.
Sara: reaching out to CS-Lead to coordinate contacting the customer ops to request expanding subnet or adding NAT.
CS-Lead: pinged the customer — they're aware, their network team is investigating adding secondary IP space; ETA unknown (they said possibly 6-12 hours).
Dmitri: immediate mitigations: traffic split + throttle + fallback should reduce customer impact. Can you confirm error rate dropped? Sara?
Sara: errors dropping to ~3% in last 5m, 95th latency down to 1.2s. Good improvement but still elevated for some long payloads.
Kevin: long term: need autoscaler to detect "ENI exhaustion" and mark cluster as "constrained" to avoid aggressive backoff and instead trigger a guided CS automation (notify customer with recommended actions). Filing infra ticket.
Maya: also saw image-pull timeouts for one of the nodes — because no NAT; even if they expand subnet, init might still fail until NAT is present or we mirror images into a subnet-accessible repo. Suggest we add a fallback AMI with preloaded images for private clusters.
Dmitri: agreed. open follow-ups: 1) infra ticket to create autoscaler signal for ENI/cidr exhaustion (INF-xxxx) 2) product/ops runbook for private VPC coldstart (PR-ops-priv-coldstart) 3) CS ticket for guidance checklist (CS-xxxx) 4) postmortem if customer impact persists.
Infra-Runner: created INF-4821: "autoscaler: recognise cloud subnet IP exhaustion and route to fallback logic" — assigned to Kevin.
Kevin: picking up INF-4821. Also will prototype an AMI/prepull image approach.
CS-Lead: created CS-9012: "cust-acme vpc subnet exhaustion - network action requested" and copied network runbook and recommended commands for their team.
Dmitri: handoff time — I need to go offline in 30m. Sara, Kevin — can you take run of actions and own incident until customer confirms network change?
Sara: I can own until 03:00 UTC, will monitor metrics and CS comms.
Kevin: I'll own the infra ticket and AMI prototype, will be on call overnight for any re-escalation.
Dmitri: thanks. summary for incident notes: root cause — customer subnet secondary IP exhaustion + absent NAT causing node boot failures -> autoscaler backoff led to queue growth -> customer errors. Mitigations applied: traffic split to fallback model, ingress throttling, manual attempts to provision alternative nodes blocked by onboarding pinning. Followups created INF-4821, CS-9012, PR-ops-priv-coldstart.
Maya: logs and command snippets uploaded to thread and incident doc: https://incidents.internal/1795007777
Dmitri: handing off to Sara and Kevin for monitoring and followups. tagging #oncall-night. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity downgraded from P0 to P1 (partial degradation, mitigations applied). Next update scheduled in 2h or on customer confirmation.
Sara: ack. will post updates in the thread if anything regresses.
